finding: The listed قَرْن and قُرُون occurrences refer to peoples or generations, while other derivatives include a companion, قَرِين, and people bound together, مُقَرَّنِينَ. These uses invite temporal or paired associations for ذو القرنين, but shared roots across different forms do not identify the title’s sense.

evidence.ar: وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنَا ٱلْقُرُونَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَمَّا ظَلَمُوا۟
قَالَ قَآئِلٌۭ مِّنْهُمْ إِنِّى كَانَ لِى قَرِينٌۭ
وَتَرَى ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ مُّقَرَّنِينَ فِى ٱلْأَصْفَادِ

missing: A lexical account of قَرْن and evidence explaining the title ذو القرنين could establish whether it refers to paired eras, horns, or another sense; the supplied occurrences do not settle this.

finding: The Form II verb occurs under divine agency elsewhere, as in 17:54, but 18:86 offers تُعَذِّبَ as Dhu al-Qarnayn’s authority. In 18:87 he takes up that option with نُعَذِّبُهُ, then distinguishes it from the punishment after the person is returned to his Lord. This frames his punishment as a bounded worldly judgment within a larger divine judgment.

evidence.ar: قَالَ أَمَّا مَن ظَلَمَ فَسَوْفَ نُعَذِّبُهُۥ ثُمَّ يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ فَيُعَذِّبُهُۥ عَذَابًۭا نُّكْرًۭا
رَّبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ ۖ إِن يَشَأْ يَرْحَمْكُمْ أَوْ إِن يَشَأْ يُعَذِّبْكُمْ

activation: The paired إِمَّا branches address Dhu al-Qarnayn, and the next ayah’s قَالَ introduces his response before the return to the person’s Lord.
limits: The passage does not specify the earthly penalty or establish a general theory of delegated rule; the distinction is explicit within this episode.

finding: Form VIII can describe adopting a person into a status or allegiance, as in 3:28 and 18:50. Here تَتَّخِذَ takes حُسْنًا as its object and فِيهِمْ marks the people as the domain: goodness is framed as an adopted course of conduct toward them. The next ayah carries this constructive branch forward with reward and ease.

evidence.ar: لَّا يَتَّخِذِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ أَوْلِيَآءَ مِن دُونِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
وَأَمَّا مَنْ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا فَلَهُۥ جَزَآءً ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ ۖ وَسَنَقُولُ لَهُۥ مِنْ أَمْرِنَا يُسْرًۭا

activation: The focus ayah pairs تَتَّخِذَ with تُعَذِّبَ as alternatives for dealing with the people; 18:88 develops the constructive branch for those who believe and act rightly.
limits: حُسْنًا leaves the particular good conduct unspecified, and the examples do not make every Form VIII use carry this moral sense.
